newsitem.title: USA: JB Hanauer names Roger Hershey to lead new dept..
newsitem.headline: JB Hanauer names Roger Hershey to lead new dept..

text.p: JB Hanauer & Co has tapped former Merrill Lynch & Co. managing director Roger Hershey to head a newly created department as director of institutional fixed income, Ken Meiselman, JB Hanauer's head trader, said Friday.
In his new position, Hershey will head institutional sales and trading for both municipal and corporate bonds, Meiselman said. The position becomes effective Monday.
"We have an institutional presence on the municipal side," the head trader said. "We hope to expand that (and) make it better."

JB Hanauer began to develop its muni institutional side about a year and a half ago, he said. The venture has worked well, and has paid off on the retail side by providing product for that sales force to sell.
While JB Hanauer does work in taxable securities, Hershey's hiring marks its first foray into the institutional sector there, Meiselman said.
"We have a great retail operation here, and we're just looking forward to having a great institutional operation as well that will work hand in hand with our retail operation," he said.
The head trader, who has known Hershey for quite some time, cited Hershey's "intelligence," "work ethic," and "enthusiam," as attributes that attracted JB Hanauer's attention.
"We view him as a winner here, and thought he could help us succeed in this venture," Meiselman said.
Hershey resigned from Merrill's municipal strategies group on Februray 14, capping a roughly 15-year career at the firm.

Meanwhile, JB Hanauer has seen some professionals depart in recent months. Beginning with Lou D'Andrea's departure in April, a total of six members of JB Hanauer's institutional sales force have departed for Livingston, N.J.-based GMS Group.
JB Hanauer is based in Parsippany, N.J.
